bibliographic.title: Multi-curve HJM modelling for risk management
bibliographic.authors: Chiara Sabelli, Michele Pioppi, Luca Sitzia, Giacomo Bormetti
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sabelli, C., Pioppi, M., Sitzia, L., & Bormetti, G. (2015). Multi-curve HJM modelling for risk management. arXiv preprint arXiv:1411.3977.

methodology.method_family: Quantitative finance; Heath-Jarrow-Morton multi-curve modeling; VAR(1) approximation; PCA dimension reduction; bootstrap estimation; out-of-sample back-testing
methodology.study_design: Model development and empirical validation on Euro area yield curves
methodology.sample_description: Historical multiple yield curves from the Euro area observed at daily frequency for a finite number of time-to-maturity buckets
methodology.technology_context: Interest rate term-structure modeling for market risk measures (VaR, Expected Shortfall); no AI, LLM, or conversational systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper is a quantitative finance preprint on multi-curve HJM interest rate modeling for financial risk management. It does not address LLMs, conversational AI, generative AI governance, guardrails, human oversight, audit/logging of AI systems, or related governance mechanisms in regulated AI contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Despite keyword overlaps from automated screening (risk management, policy, standard, bias, review, framework), the substantive content concerns yield curve forecasting, volatility-correlation structure, and financial risk measures in the Euro area. There is no evidence of conversational systems, large language models, or AI governance/accountability frameworks relevant to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is unambiguous from title, abstract, and full-text excerpts; false-positive governance terms refer to statistical bias, monetary policy, and standard model formulation.

appraisal.notes: Methodological quality appears adequate for quantitative finance risk modeling, but the study is outside the review domain. Appraisal reflects only signals present in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: For the systematic review on conversational governance of LLMs in regulated settings, relevance is very low. The paper coherently addresses financial yield-curve risk modeling but provides no usable evidence on AI governance, conversational systems, or LLM-specific controls.

coding.subtheme: Multi-curve interest rate dynamics and forecasting

synthesis.main_claim: A discrete HJM-based multi-curve modeling framework, approximated by VAR(1) and simplified with PCA, can capture historical term-structure volatility and support feasible estimation of volatility-correlation structure and market risk premia for financial risk management forecasting.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a feasible discrete-time multi-curve HJM approach with demonstrated out-of-sample forecasting ability on Euro area curves for risk management applications such as VaR and Expected Shortfall.
synthesis.limitations: Model inadequacies appear for more extreme coverage probabilities and longer horizons, especially shortest EONIA maturities; Brownian-shock dynamics struggle to reproduce discrete ECB policy shifts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude. May serve only as an illustrative false-positive example of keyword-based screening confusion between financial risk management and AI governance risk.

evidence.claim: Paper topic is financial yield-curve risk modeling, not AI or conversational governance
evidence.excerpt: We present a HJM approach to the projection of multiple yield curves developed to capture the volatility content of historical term structures for risk management purposes.

evidence.claim: Financial risk management context with VaR and Expected Shortfall, not AI governance
evidence.excerpt: expected exposures of portfolios made of such instruments and in turn risk measures like VaR and Expected Shortfall are tightly related to the future distributions of underlying interest rates

evidence.claim: No LLM or conversational AI technology context
evidence.excerpt: we show how to approximate the HJM continuous time description of the multi-curve dynamics by a Vector Autoregressive process of order one

evidence.claim: Automated 'bias' hit refers to statistical estimation bias, not AI fairness bias
evidence.excerpt: Conditionally on the non existence of a significant bias between the historical estimate and the bootstrap mean

evidence.claim: Automated 'policy' hits refer to ECB monetary policy, not AI/compliance policy
evidence.excerpt: the monetary policy of the European Central Bank (ECB) largely determines curve dynamics

evidence.claim: Study applies model to Euro area curves with out-of-sample testing
evidence.excerpt: Applying the constant volatility version of our model on a sample of curves from the Euro area, we demonstrate its forecasting ability through an out-of-sample test.
